Renée Zellweger, Dominic Sessa and Peter Dinklage Set for Sacha Gervasi's 'Darlington,' Launching Foreign Sales at AFM

29 Oct 2026, 06:39 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Entertainment Desk · Source: deadline.com

Cast and Creative Team Announced for 'Darlington'

Two-time Oscar winner Renée Zellweger will star alongside Dominic Sessa and Peter Dinklage in Darlington, a high-concept comedy drama directed by Sacha Gervasi, according to Deadline. The project is set to launch foreign sales at the American Film Market (AFM), with a spring production in the UK currently in the works.

The film is a Rocket Science, Monumental Pictures, and Portobello Electric production. Alison Owen and Debra Hayward are producing for Monumental Pictures, while Jim Garavente produces for Portobello Electric. Alexander Payne serves as executive producer.

Plot and Characters

Gervasi wrote the screenplay, which centers on Kate Spencer, played by Zellweger. Kate is described as a faded television actress long forgotten by the industry who receives an invitation to reprise her most famous role. However, the opportunity is not a conventional revival or reboot. Instead, she is invited into the real world of a reclusive tech billionaire, played by Sessa, who has meticulously restored an English country estate to its former glory. Having withdrawn from public life, the billionaire lives under the fantasy that it is still 1923. As Kate settles into this controlled environment, she discovers that illusion and reality are more entwined than she imagined.

Dinklage, a longtime Gervasi collaborator, also stars, though his specific character was not detailed in the announcement.

Background on the Filmmakers and Cast

Gervasi is a British writer and director whose credits include co-writing Steven Spielberg's The Terminal, starring Tom Hanks and Catherine Zeta-Jones. His directorial debut, Anvil! The Story of Anvil (2008), premiered at Sundance and won the Independent Spirit Award for Best Documentary. He later directed the Academy Award-nominated Hitchcock and wrote and directed HBO's My Dinner with Hervé, which starred Dinklage and earned a Primetime Emmy nomination for Outstanding Television Movie.

Zellweger recently starred in and executive produced Mad About the Boy, the final chapter in the Bridget Jones franchise, and is currently in production on A Woman in the Sun. Sessa, a BAFTA nominee for The Holdovers and Tony, is currently filming Miami Vice '85.

What Is Confirmed and What Remains Unknown

Confirmed:

  • Zellweger, Sessa, and Dinklage are attached to star.
  • Gervasi is directing his own screenplay.
  • Foreign sales will begin at AFM.
  • A UK spring production is planned.
  • Producers include Alison Owen, Debra Hayward, and Jim Garavente; Alexander Payne is executive producer.

Unknown or not yet disclosed:

  • A specific production start date or release window.
  • The full cast beyond the three leads.
  • Dinklage's character details.
  • Financing or budget information.
  • Distribution or streaming plans.

How Readers Can Verify the Announcement

The original report was published by Deadline and is available at https://deadline.com/2026/10/renee-zellweger-dominic-sessa-peter-dinklage-darlington-1237207085/. Readers can review the full announcement there for the complete list of production credits and representation details included in the source.

Practical Implications

For industry observers, the AFM launch signals that international distribution rights are actively being packaged ahead of production. The involvement of Monumental Pictures producers Alison Owen and Debra Hayward, whose credits include Back to Black and Les Misérables, alongside executive producer Alexander Payne, suggests the film is positioned as an independent prestige project rather than a major studio tentpole. For audiences, the premise—a faded actress entering a billionaire's 1923 fantasy—positions Darlington as a character-driven comedy drama with potential awards-season relevance, though no festival or release plans have been announced.

Comparisons can be drawn to Gervasi's previous work with Dinklage on My Dinner with Hervé and to Zellweger's recent return to the Bridget Jones franchise, though Darlington is an original screenplay and not part of an existing franchise.
